claims.claim: Rotation is stronger in clusters with longer relaxation times — primordial spin survives where two-body relaxation is slow (trend, no coefficient quoted).
claims.source: Bianchini et al. 2018; Kamann et al. 2018; Sollima et al. 2019 (weak, <3sigma)
claims.ours: CONFIRMED and sharpened: V/sigma vs half-light radius rho=+0.71 (p=0.004) in our reliable subset — size and relaxation time go hand in hand.

claims.claim: More massive (brighter, higher-dispersion) clusters rotate more strongly.
claims.source: Bianchini et al. 2018; Fabricius et al. 2014; Bellazzini et al. 2012
claims.ours: Consistent direction: V/sigma vs log N members rho=+0.45 (p=0.038, full sample).

claims.claim: Metal-rich clusters rotate faster (significant but secondary correlation, ~25 GCs, LOS velocities).
claims.source: Bellazzini et al. 2012 (also Kacharov et al. 2014)
claims.ours: NOT confirmed: rho = 0.0 in our PM-based sample of 22 measurable clusters — an interesting disagreement worth discussing.

claims.claim: Disputed in the literature: Fabricius et al. 2014 and Kamann et al. 2018 report rotating clusters are more flattened; Sollima et al. 2019 and Bellazzini et al. 2012 find no link.
claims.ours: Not measured — our target list has no ellipticity column (future work).

claims.claim: Clusters being destroyed fastest by Galactic tides have lost the most angular momentum (anticorrelation, <3sigma).
claims.ours: Not measured directly, but motivates our tidal-stripping side study.

claims.claim: Maximum PM rotation signals range from ~0.5 km/s up to ~6 km/s for NGC 104 and NGC 5139.
claims.ours: MATCHED almost exactly: our V_peak = 6.15 km/s (NGC 104) and 6.09 km/s (NGC 5139).

note: Published V/sigma from Bianchini et al. 2018 Table 1 (Gaia DR2 PMs). Differences in absolute V/sigma partly reflect different definitions of V and sigma; rank order is the fairer comparison.
